rule.reference_R: MeikiOCR 0.3.5's detector (meiki.text.detect.v0.1, sha256 40b6a016..., threshold 0.5, its own fit to 960x544, BGR) on the whole frame; each box grown by eval/desktop.py's auto pad (4 px on a 960x544-class frame, 2 px on a native PSP frame) and read by VOCR6.2_L_fast.onnx (v0.5.1-onnx.2), greedy CTC, no LM, no line filter
rule.candidate_C: the desktop detector (train/desktop_det.py, tools/vocr_desktop.py) at an input-size policy, read the same way by VOCR6.2_L_fast.onnx
rule.metric: dialogue CER of eval/desktop.py read: every box whose centre lies in a unit's region, in reading order, against the unit's references (eval/pagepath.py score_unit); VN clusters on dev / confirm, title clusters on hval; eval/pagepath.py cluster_bootstrap (10,000, seed 0)
rule.accuracy: dev-v2: CER(C) <= 1.20 x CER(R) for the representative seed (the median of 3 seeds by dev-v2 CER at fit:960); the paired 95% interval of CER(C) - CER(R) not entirely above 0; the Vita view and the PSP view each CER(C) <= 1.5 x CER(R) of that view
rule.guards: hval (title clusters) and confirm-v2 (VN clusters, read once for the candidate set after the dev decision is recorded): CER(C) - CER(R) not resolved above 0
rule.speed: eval/desktop_time.py run at 4 intra-op threads, mode par (the detector at 4 threads, the lines on 4 Python threads sharing one recognizer session at 1 thread), interleaved with R in the same run, on the timing pages: p50 ms per page of C <= 1/4 of R's, on the Vita and on the PSP timing pages separately
rule.pick: each input-size policy of the chosen arm (fit:960, fit:800, fit:640, fit:480) is a candidate; among those that pass accuracy, guards and speed, the cheapest (p50 at 4 threads, Vita + PSP) is the pick; a costlier one replaces it only when it is resolved better on dev-v2
rule.seeds: 3 seeds of the chosen arm for the adoption claim; screening on hval with 1 seed
rule.then: the pick ships: the chosen arm retrained with the representative seed on train + guard + hval (the final model); its own dev-v2 score is reported; the test titles are read once with it. No qualifier: the measurements are published with the gap and what would close it

S4_d48_single.role: report only: the single-scale control (trained near one text size, then read at other input sizes, as the dynamic-size MeikiOCR variant was): the per-size accuracy against S1 shows what the multi-scale training buys

screening.rule: on hval at fit:960 (R's pipeline otherwise): the multi-scale arm (S1-S3) with the lowest CER; an arm within 0.10 points of the lowest that is cheaper (MACs at 960x544) replaces it
screening.data: data/manifests/desktop_pages_v21.json (train split; textspot6_pages.py on pagepool v2.1 with MeikiOCR's boxes for the text the hook does not cover), data/manifests/textspot_shards_v1.json (synthetic frames), data/manifests/textspot2_shards_v1.json (MeikiOCR-labelled VNDB / owner screenshots outside the dev sample) with its skip lists

hval.note: the hval pages of hooked pools v2.1 (b2-ingest2 #166, pagepool v2.1 bbadfcbf), base dialogue regions; screening only

dev.note: "dev-v2": #119 units (base variant) without the 9 VNs pools v2.1 trains on; the decision set

confirm.note: "confirm-v2": textspot7 confirmation units (base) without the 4 VNs pools v2.1 trains on; read once, at the end, for the candidate set

pc.note: the dev units cut from PC screenshots, at the screenshots own size; report only

test.what: the hooked test titles index.json marks test (pagepool v2.1 split test), base dialogue regions, native frames
test.when: once, after the final model exists and the dev-v2 decision record is committed; R, C (the pick), MeikiOCR itself and textspot8 + VOCR6.2-L

timing.pages: eval/desktop_time.py pages --seed 20261101: 60 Vita-view and 60 PSP-view frames of dev-v2, 30 PC-sample frames
timing.method: eval/desktop_time.py run: passes 3 after 1 warm-up, the pipelines in a shuffled order each pass, a page's time the median of its passes; threads 1, 2, 4 in one heavy slot each, 8 in two

not_read: vita-test, psp-test, CLANNAD (never); the test titles until the attempt above

amendments.before: any candidate is timed or scored (the screening runs S1_d48 / S2_d64 are at step 1600 of 40,000; no candidate box has been read)
amendments.what: the speed clause's thread budget: 'at 4 threads' is a budget of 4. Each pipeline's detector runs at the intra-op thread count in {1, 2, 4} that gives it the lowest p50 on that view's timing pages in the same run (R's MeikiOCR detector included); its lines run par on 4 Python threads sharing one recognizer session at 1 intra-op thread, as before (eval/desktop_time.py run --threads 4 with the pipelines' '#d1', '#d2', '#d4' variants)
amendments.why: the baseline profile (eval/desktop_time.py profile, ORT kernel ms per run, ORT_ENABLE_ALL, 1 -> 4 intra-op threads, this shared host) shows the thread pool slowing the small graphs: textspot8 exact 8.09 -> 11.74 ms, VOCR6.2-L fast 2.35 -> 2.38 ms, while MeikiOCR's detector gains 1.73x (102.0 -> 59.1 ms). Forcing 4 intra-op threads on a graph that runs slower with them would measure the thread pool, not the model; R's detector is fastest at 4 threads, so R keeps its measured time
